finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF/arbitrary URL and file read: POST 'feed' is passed directly to file_get_contents, which fetches http(s)://, ftp://, file://, php:// wrappers. The response length is echoed back, giving a blind/oracle channel (internal service reachability, file existence/size, cloud metadata).

trace.note: Only checks request method is POST and 'feed' is set; no auth
User value passed straight to file_get_contents (URL wrapper fetch)
strlen of fetched body echoed to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No require_admin() call on this path (it is only used in the webhook branch), no scheme/host allowlist, no private-IP/metadata blocking, no redirect handling. Nothing found.

verdict.reason: import.php:11-13 passes unauthenticated $_POST['feed'] directly to file_get_contents and echoes strlen of the result, with no require_admin() (only called at line 18 in the webhook branch) and no scheme or host validation.

finding.claim: SSRF via admin webhook setting: user-supplied URL is requested server-side with curl, with no scheme/host validation. Curl supports http, https, gopher, file, ftp, etc. and follows no restriction on internal addresses. Requires admin session, which lowers severity, but admin-controlled URL still reaches internal network/metadata.

trace.note: Branch entered when set_webhook is posted

finding.guards_checked: require_admin() session check (present, limits to admins); no URL scheme, host allowlist, or internal IP filtering; CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS not set. Response not returned (blind SSRF).

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() session check at import.php:4-9 (admin-only gate); no URL scheme/host validation
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (import.php:17-22), but the URL reaching curl_init at import.php:20 is only reachable after require_admin() at import.php:18, so the source is admin-only and not controllable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker.
